headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: RD-Agent’s broad API/browser egress can expose EMQX IoT data if paired workflows share outputs without verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between EMQX and RD-Agent, so direct prompt injection is not established. However, RD-Agent can run browsers and EMQX exposes an HTTP API, so if operators manually bridge outputs through files or copied content, injected instructions could be carried across. The pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies EMQX-served content into RD-Agent prompts or browser tasks, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared file or message channel is introduced between the agents, attacker-controlled text can traverse it.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable manual copy-paste between agent outputs and prompts.
Strip instructions from any EMQX-derived text before reuse.
Use a human review step for any cross-agent content transfer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data and has broad network egress; RD-Agent touches financial reports, papers, datasets, logs, and sends data to third-party APIs such as OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, DeepSeek, and Kaggle. If the pair shares a workspace or if EMQX outputs are fed into RD-Agent, sensitive IoT data can be uploaded off-box in default-style workflows. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF EMQX outputs containing IoT data are passed into RD-Agent prompts or files, leakage risk increases.
IF RD-Agent is configured to process shared logs or datasets from EMQX, those contents may reach external APIs.
mitigations: Do not place both agents in the same writable workspace.
Redact IoT identifiers before any transfer to RD-Agent.
Block outbound API calls for RD-Agent during cross-agent analysis.
Review logs for accidental inclusion of EMQX payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: EMQX has HTTP API access and broad network egress, while RD-Agent has broad network egress, browser use, and multiple-instance support. There is no evidence of shared filesystem write or overlapping mutable resource ownership, so direct write conflict is not shown. The main overlap is network-side, which is weaker than the rubric’s medium/high conflict cases.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable HTTP endpoint, they can race on remote state.
IF an operator gives both agents write access to the same external service, conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per agent.
Serialize writes to any shared remote service.
Use a lock or queue around shared endpoints.
Prefer read-only access for one agent during analysis.

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent is a scientific-research agent that can browse and call multiple external APIs, so it may treat EMQX-produced outputs as inputs for downstream analysis or actions. EMQX can emit API-accessible content, but no verification boundary between the pair is documented. That makes a mistaken EMQX output plausibly cascade into RD-Agent’s reports or API calls.
conditions: IF RD-Agent consumes EMQX output without an explicit verification step, errors can propagate.
IF RD-Agent uses EMQX-derived facts in reports or API-driven workflows, downstream mistakes can multiply.
mitigations: Require source verification before RD-Agent uses EMQX outputs.
Mark EMQX outputs as untrusted in prompts and files.
Add a human approval step before any downstream action.
Keep a provenance note with each transferred artifact.

E_compliance.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, logs, and sends data to third-party APIs. The profiles do not specify residency or regulatory certifications, so a compliance mismatch cannot be ruled out. Because the data classes are sensitive and the external API path is explicit, the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF IoT data includes regulated personal data, and RD-Agent sends it to external APIs, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF either agent is used on data subject to residency or retention rules, the mismatch becomes material.
mitigations: Classify the data before transfer.
Exclude regulated records from RD-Agent inputs.
Confirm vendor terms for each external API.
Set short retention for logs and outputs.
